answer: Reputation-decay cost curve. Each identity's influence decays like a glacier: slow at first, then sharply after 30 idle days, so mass registration yields near-zero weight. New identities must fund a hollow escrow that refills only through verified transactions, and rewards shrink by a delta per sibling identity sharing the same funding source. Attackers pay escalating escrow plus sustained activity costs across every fake identity, making N sybils cost roughly N² in locked capital and upkeep.
